related_questions.question: What does custody mean in finance?

text_blocks.snippet: In finance, custody refers to the safekeeping of assets, typically financial assets like securities, on behalf of a client by a financial institution. A custodian is responsible for holding these assets securely and for administering related services like trade settlement, income collection, and reporting.

list.title: Safekeeping:
list.snippet: The primary function of custody is to ensure the physical or electronic safekeeping of client assets.

list.title: Administration:
list.snippet: Custodians also handle various administrative tasks related to the assets, such as settling trades, collecting income (like dividends or interest), and managing corporate actions.

list.title: Record Keeping:
list.snippet: Accurate and timely record-keeping of all transactions and asset movements is a crucial part of custody.

list.title: Not Investment Decisions:
list.snippet: While custodians are responsible for safekeeping and administering assets, they do not make investment decisions for the client. This is typically the role of the investment advisor or manager.

list.title: Types of Custodians:
list.snippet: Custodians can be banks, trust companies, or brokerage firms.

list.title: Custodial Accounts:
list.snippet: A custodial account is a financial account established for the benefit of a minor or other beneficiary, with a custodian managing the assets.

text_blocks.snippet: In essence, custody is about protecting and managing assets on behalf of a client, ensuring their safety and facilitating their proper handling within the financial system.
